posts.title: Architecting Enterprise AI Workflows with LiteLLM, Langfuse, and OpenBao
posts.author: Nguyen Huynh Huy Man
posts.summary: How to deploy and orchestrate Human-in-the-Loop AI automation workflows on Red Hat OpenShift using LiteLLM proxy, Langfuse observability, and OpenBao secrets vault.
posts.contentHtml:
As generative AI and autonomous agents transition from experimental pilots into core enterprise business operations, platform teams face new challenges in model governance, cost monitoring, latency optimization, and secret management.

In this post, we explore the architecture of a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) automation pipeline deployed across an enterprise Red Hat OpenShift cluster.

Core Components of the Architecture

  1. LiteLLM Gateway: Provides a unified OpenAI-compatible API layer across multiple providers (Azure AI Foundry, Anthropic, Bedrock, and self-hosted models).

  2. Langfuse Telemetry: Captures full execution traces, token consumption, model latencies, and evaluations.

  3. OpenBao Secrets Vault: Open-source fork of HashiCorp Vault ensuring encrypted, ephemeral credential brokering.

  4. Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Controller: Leverages GitHub Actions and GitHub Issues for human approval gates before executing critical operational tasks.

Standardizing through a centralized gateway like LiteLLM decouples internal client applications from specific vendor APIs, enabling seamless fallbacks and automatic failover during downstream outages.

Deploying LiteLLM on OpenShift

Below is a declarative OpenShift Deployment configuration with health checks and resource constraints: 

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: litellm-proxy
  namespace: ai-platform
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: litellm-proxy
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: litellm-proxy
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: litellm
        image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 4000
        env:
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: ai-platform-secrets
              key: database-url
        - name: STORE_MODEL_IN_DB
          value: "True"
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "1Gi"
          limits:
            cpu: "2"
            memory: "4Gi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/readiness
            port: 4000
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 10

Instrumenting Langfuse Observability

Tracking input/output tokens and cost attribution across engineering squads is mandatory for enterprise FinOps: 

import os
from langfuse.openai import openai

# Automatic tracing hooked via OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM proxy
openai.api_base = os.getenv("LITELLM_ENDPOINT", "https://litellm.internal.domain/v1")
openai.api_key = os.getenv("LITELLM_KEY")

def execute_agent_step(prompt: str, session_id: str) -> str:
    response = openai.ChatCompletion.create(
        model="azure-gpt4o",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        metadata={
            "session_id": session_id,
            "environment": "production",
            "tier": "enterprise-agent"
        }
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content

Summary of Takeaways

By combining OpenShift's robust container scheduling with specialized LLMOps tooling:

  • Teams gained real-time visibility into latency and cost via Langfuse.

  • API keys are rotated dynamically through OpenBao, mitigating credential leaks.

  • The organization established a standardized, provider-agnostic AI platform ready for scale.

posts.title: Building Scalable GitOps Delivery Pipelines with ArgoCD and GitHub ARC
posts.author: Nguyen Huynh Huy Man
posts.summary: A deep dive into engineering resilient, self-healing GitOps pipelines using ArgoCD, Actions Runner Controller (ARC), and multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters.
posts.contentHtml:
GitOps has fundamentally shifted how cloud-native engineering teams manage infrastructure and application lifecycles. By treating Git repositories as the single source of truth for declarative infrastructure, platforms achieve enhanced auditability, automated drift detection, and reproducible environments.

In this article, we examine an enterprise architecture combining ArgoCD with GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC) to eliminate build queue bottlenecks and establish continuous reconciliation.

Architectural Objectives

When designing multi-tenant CI/CD platforms across staging and production clusters, three challenges dominate:

  1. Runner Sprawl & Idle Costs: Fixed static build agents incur ongoing cloud compute overhead during idle periods.

  2. Configuration Drift: Imperative deployments via ad-hoc scripts lead to divergence between environments.

  3. Security Boundaries: Providing deployment credentials directly inside CI runners expands the blast radius of potential compromises.

Key Principle: The CI pipeline should only build artifacts and update deployment manifests in Git. It should never hold direct cluster-admin credentials. ArgoCD pulls and reconciles cluster state internally.

Autoscaling CI with GitHub ARC

The GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC) deploys an operator in the Kubernetes cluster that spins up ephemeral runner pods on demand based on GitHub webhook metrics: 

apiVersion: actions.summerwind.dev/v1alpha1
kind: RunnerDeployment
metadata:
  name: k8s-arc-runner
  namespace: arc-runners
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      repository: org/cloud-platform
      dockerdWithinRunner: false
      nodeSelector:
        workload: ci-compute
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "4"
          memory: "8Gi"
        requests:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: "2Gi"
---
apiVersion: actions.summerwind.dev/v1alpha1
kind: HorizontalRunnerAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: k8s-arc-runner-autoscaler
  namespace: arc-runners
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: k8s-arc-runner
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics:
  - type: PercentageRunnersBusy
    scaleUpThreshold: '0.75'
    scaleDownThreshold: '0.3'
    scaleUpFactor: '1.5'

Declarative Deployment with ArgoCD

Once the CI runner pushes a new image tag to the container registry and updates the target Git environment repo, ArgoCD triggers automated reconciliation: 

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: platform-portal
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: 'https://github.com/org/gitops-manifests.git'
    targetRevision: HEAD
    path: envs/production
  destination:
    server: 'https://kubernetes.default.svc'
    namespace: production
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true
    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=true

Performance Metrics & Results

Metric

Before (Static Agents)

After (ARC + GitOps)

Average Build Wait Time

8.5 minutes

25 seconds

Deployment Drift Incident Rate

14% monthly

0% (auto-healed)

Cloud Compute Idle Cost

100% baseline

Reduced by 58%

Conclusion

Decoupling continuous integration (handled by ephemeral, containerized runners) from continuous delivery (enforced by declarative GitOps controllers) yields a hardened, scalable foundation. Engineering teams regain velocity without sacrificing infrastructure compliance.
